service.name: Acoustic duo and trio
service.serviceType: Acoustic duo and trio for cocktail hours, dinner parties, patios and welcome drinks
service.description: Voice and guitar, guitar and upright bass, or the trio joining all three musicians, playing singer-songwriter and folk-rock covers at conversation volume for cocktail hours, dinner parties and receptions across Denver and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the acoustic duo and the jazz duo?
faqs.a: The repertoire. The acoustic duo plays singer-songwriter and folk-rock covers, songs guests know the words to. The jazz duo plays standards. Footprint, volume and price are the same, so the choice comes down to what the crowd should hear.

Voice and guitar when the songs should be sung, which suits cocktail hours, patios and welcome drinks. Guitar and upright bass when you want the set instrumental, which usually suits dinner. The price is the same either way, and so is the volume: 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table.

faqs.q: Can the acoustic duo play outside?
faqs.a: Yes, and patios are its regular work. It needs a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it, and we agree a move-indoors plan with you ahead of time. Colorado evenings cool fast, and instruments and electronics both stop behaving in the cold and the wet.

faqs.q: How long can the duo play?
faqs.a: Sets run 45 to 60 minutes with 15 to 20 between them, built around the flow of your evening, and audio continues through breaks so the night never goes silent. If the night runs long, we can add time in half-hour blocks.

faqs.q: Does the acoustic duo book as a trio?
faqs.a: Yes. The acoustic trio puts voice, guitar and upright bass on the same night, so you get both the sung set and the instrumental set. It books for a single hour or a whole evening, just like the duo. When the night should grow past three, the same booking can grow to a quartet on one contract.
